transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Nguyen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Casey Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Mariner Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Infra), Marta Silva (Product)

Auto summary (auto-generated, maybe rough):
- Bench contrasts vs incumbent: Redwood shows lower p95 latency on small-chat model and higher sustained qps in multi-tenant bursts.
- Key tuning: routing thresholds, KV cache warmup, quantization profile 4/8 mix for cost tradeoff.
- Next actions: share spreadsheet, run extended dedicated slot, security deep-dive.

Topics:
- Raw numbers: p50/p95/p99, qps, failure rates
- Routing playbook: fallback to smaller model when latency > threshold
- Dedicated slot request and scheduling
- Data/infra needs for 24h run and logs
- Security questions (KMS, audit logs, SOC 2)

Transcript (selected excerpts, timestamps every ~30-60s):
[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll go through the bench contrasts versus your incumbent and then we can talk tuning and next steps. Priya, Ethan, Marta, thanks for making time.
[00:14] Priya: yep thanks, we got a busy week but wanted to see the delta, we ran your smoke harness yesterday and the initial numbers look good but we had questions.
[00:22] Diego: cool quick note, the smoke run was on the 7B chat model variant with kv-cache on and the 4-bit quant profile, ok? so numbers are apples-to-our-config not exact to your prod model but close.
[00:36] Ethan: quick clarification — when you say kv-cache on that means the prefix cache for session tokens? we saw some cache misses earlier.
[00:44] Diego: right it's the prefix/K V cache — the cache warmup matters if you do cold sessions, we saw miss-rate drop after 30s of steady traffic.
[00:51] Marta: the big thing for product is latency p95 under 250ms for ui flows, that's our bar.
[00:58] Diego: to be explicit, baseline (IncumbentCloudAI) you reported p95 around 210ms but throughput flattened at ~90 qps under sustained bursts. In our lab, Redwood measured p95 ~150ms and sustained qps ~125 at the same concurrency, with p99 spikes near 380ms during cold starts.
[01:20] Priya: those p95 numbers look promising, can you walk through how you measured? was it single region? multi-az?
[01:27] Sofia: yeah measured in our us-east cluster with single region routing; the harness used 80/20 short/long prompts to mimic your mix. Full CSV will show per-prompt buckets.
[01:36] Ethan: I saw a note about latency vs cost tradeoff, the team is sensitive — if we get 25% lower latency but cost goes up 15% that's a hard sell.
[01:46] Diego: totally — that's where quantization and routing help. For example, using 4-bit for short prompts and 8-bit for long ones we keep cost near baseline while improving latency on short flows. We can also route heavy tails to a cheaper model when not in UI-critical path.
[02:02] Priya: do you have numbers for the mixed quantization approach?
[02:05] Diego: preliminary: mixed quant shaving gives ~8-12% cost over baseline but reduces p95 for UI prompts by ~18-22%. We'll include exact rows.
[02:13] Marta: what about dedicated vs hosted? we're leaning private but timeline is tight.
[02:17] Sofia: recommended path: start hosted POC to prove perf and cost, then move to dedicated reserved pools for production. For timeline, we can provision temporary dedicated slots for higher isolation and then migrate.
[02:28] Ethan: what's the lead time for a dedicated slot?
[02:31] Diego: we can spin up a temporary dedicated pool within 48 hours once you sign the pilot addendum; permanent reserved capacity takes longer, but for a 24h smoke run we can do it fast.
[02:41] Priya: you mentioned fallback routing when capacity is constrained — how transparent is that? will requests get different models and will that break behavior?
[02:50] Diego: fallback is policy-driven; you can choose to fallback only for non-UI calls or use A/B to sample. Semantically, smaller models have slightly different output but we can do safety/regression checks against your eval set. There's a rollout knob.
[03:05] Marta: any security red flags from our end? we need KMS, SSO, audit logs, retention controls.
[03:10] Casey: quick answer — we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments, SAML SSO for console, and deliver audit logs with configurable retention; we will schedule a security deep-dive next week for specifics.
[03:21] Ethan: in the smoke logs we saw 4xx errors around bursts, was that rate limiting?
[03:25] Diego: yes that was our default per-connection limiter kicking in on the harness burst; we adjusted autoscale and limits in the second run — errors dropped to <0.5%. We'll annotate the CSV.
[03:35] Priya: curious about p99 behavior — you called out p99 spikes near 380ms, in prod we care about tail beyond 500ms.
[03:42] Diego: p99 in our small-run was 380ms but with cold-start windows. With cache warm and routing thresholds tuned, p99 goes down; we'll show a warmed-run where p99 < 420ms. For your target >500ms, we should run a longer 24h test and a traffic pattern closer to your hours.
[04:00] Sofia: proposed plan — we provision a 24h dedicated run on dec 15, you provide traces and we run both cold and warmed phases, capture latency buckets and token cost.
[04:09] Priya: sounds good. also, can you share the raw logs? our infra needs to map traces to spans.
[04:14] Diego: yes raw perf logs and a Jupyter-ready CSV. I'll also include the harness config so you can reproduce.
[04:21] Ethan: if we set a routing threshold of 200ms for UI, what happens mid-burst?
[04:26] Diego: policy can route to smaller model when estimated queue/buffer > threshold; we can also auto-scale aggressively to avoid falling back. There's a cost hit for aggressive scaling.
[04:35] Marta: what about cache eviction — did you see any detrimental eviction rates?
[04:39] Diego: eviction was modest; most sessions had steady prefix reuse. For longer contexts we recommend sticky pins or KV pre-warm for anticipated flows.
[04:48] Priya: any notable differences vs EdgeServe? they flagged multitenant isolation concerns.
[04:53] Sofia: EdgeServe's elastic bins sometimes cause noisy neighbor but in our tests Redwood's routing isolates customer capacity when on dedicated pools; hosted multi-tenant has soft isolation but configurable burst reservations.
[05:05] Ethan: ok will the dedicated test require network changes on our side?
[05:09] Diego: minimal — for private you need VPC peering and a small firewall rule; for hosted dedicated, you just configure endpoints and allow the outbound. We'll send the ops note.
[05:18] Priya: last thing—how do you measure cost? tokens + gpu-hour amortization?
[05:22] Sofia: unit economics exported in the CSV: token-level cost, model gpu-second cost, and per-request amortized infra. We show cost delta vs baseline both token-normalized and per-session.
[05:33] Marta: would like to see an ROI slide that maps to our monthly active users; can you do a short model?
[05:38] Sofia: yes we'll include a simple ROI calc in the follow-up.
[05:41] Priya: great. any blockers on our side?
[05:44] Ethan: just getting traces and a PO for the temporary slot — procurement is slow but we can handle a small commitment for the test.
[05:52] Diego: if procurement delays, we can run a hosted extended test and still get meaningful warmed-run numbers; dedicated gives cleaner isolation but hosted is fine for initial validation.
[06:02] Sofia: ok recap of next steps and owners — action items we'll post in the calendar invite and Dropbox link.
[06:08] Priya: thanks all, looking forward to the CSV.
[06:11] Sofia: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and the dedicated slot confirmation by Monday.

End of transcript.
